answer_1.quote: In this work, we examine instead whether LLMs can be used to generate explicit and task-specific world models expressed as code, providing a more formal and interpretable method to examine a model's world knowledge.
answer_1.outputs: Python code implementing interactive text games

answer_2.quote: We develop a suite of metrics to assess the quality of generated games, including measuring technical aspects of the code, whether a game contains required content, how accurately a game models the physical world, and whether a game is winnable. We show that most of these metrics can be automated.

answer_3.quote: Compliance is measured automatically by supplying the generated game and its task specification to a GPT-4 model, which is then asked a series of true-or-false questions about the presence of each required component... These trajectories are then provided to GPT-4, with a prompt to provide a binary assessment as to whether the game playthrough up to that point adheres to physical reality.
methods: Automated winnability evaluation using GPT-4 agent

answer_4.quote: We compare GPT-4 ratings with gold ratings generated by two expert human annotators... Manual evaluation was performed by a single human evaluator... Human evaluations were used for specification compliance and winnability.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators rated each generated game for specification compliance (object, action, distractor inclusion) and for winnability (whether a winning sequence exists).
